text:
Morgan: Heads-up — after landing the INT8-KV option in the canary pool I see ~12% median decode latency improvement and ~18% KV memory reduction on p4-dedicated tests, but a small fraction of requests exhibit decode drift (more repetition / missing stop tokens).
Anya: ugh. can you paste the repro prompt and the perf profile? is it tied to seq length or model size?
Morgan: short repro attached inline. seems correlated with long prefix (>1500 tokens) + batch size >1. repro prompt: 'user: summarize long chat and list action items'. Behavior: sometimes repeats last sentence and never emits <|endoftext|>.
Devin: do we have profiling traces for both FP8-KV and INT8-KV for the same requests? kernel selection could be falling back to a slower path for certain seq lens.
perf-bot: perf run: https://perf.internal/runs/1762001100 (canary-int8-kv vs canary-fp8-kv). p50 p95 latency down ~12% int8, memory ~18% lower. p99 shows a tail spike coincident with "kv_spill" events.
Ravi: quick hypothesis — the "spill" kernel disables prefix-KV fast-path (we recompute attention keys instead of using optimized KV fetch), so any misclassification of kernel choice would both slow and change numerical ordering a bit, leading to decode drift.
Anya: also worth noting quant calibration: with 500 calibration steps we see slightly noisier scales; bumping to 5k steps tightened distributions and reduced decode anomalies in offline eval (perp delta -0.6 -> -0.2).
Morgan: here's the runtime config we used on canary:
```json
{
  "kv_quant": "int8",
  "calibration_steps": 500,
  "batching_mode": "adaptive",
  "kernel_thresholds": {"int8": 1024, "fp8": 2048},
  "kv_spill_enabled": true
}
```
Anya: two actionable items: 1) increase calibration_steps to 5k for INT8-KV and rerun eval harness; 2) change kernel selection to prefer FP8 path for prefix_len > 1024 to avoid triggering spill kernel that disables KV fast-path.
Devin: +1. also add a batching rule: do not merge requests where request.meta.cached_prefix == true — merging cached+uncached seems to cause the runtime to allocate shared KV buffers and triggers a fallback in a codepath we haven't hardened for quantized KV.
Ravi: I ran a quick microbench — when we hit the spill kernel, decode noise (measured as LM token entropy shift) increases by ~0.8% relative to the optimized KV fetch path. Not huge but enough to affect boundary tokens like STOP.
Morgan: thanks. I'll push a canary with calibration_steps=5000 and kernel_thresholds.int8=2048 and disable merging cached_prefix in adaptive batching.
Anya: please also add an A/B test tag so we can collect quality metrics (stop-token rate, repetition score) in telemetry. set rollout to 10% initially.
perf-bot: canary deployed: canary/kv-int8-cal5k-kthresh2048 (rollout=10%). monitoring page: https://monitoring.internal/kv-int8-cal5k
Devin: I'll run the full decoding regression harness overnight and post results. if this fixes it we can promote and update docs about safe kernel thresholds and batching rules.
Ravi: if problems persist, we should try FP8-KV as a fallback for long-prefix heavy workloads — better numeric stability, slightly higher memory.
Morgan: tagging @infra on callouts about kernel selection change (might affect autotuner heuristics). anyone volunteer to watch the A/B metrics tomorrow morning?
Anya: I can take the 8–11am PT window.
Devin: I'll triage the harness logs after my run and open a follow-up issue with exact repro cases.
Morgan: awesome — will post follow-ups in this thread. :thumbsup:
